g.text: Participatory budgeting, put to work: Porto Alegre

text.style: font-style: italic; font-size: 7.4px; font-family: 'Lora', 'Newsreader', 'Georgia', 'DejaVu Serif', serif; fill: #8a857b

g.text: Porto Alegre, Brazil adopted participatory budgeting in 1989. Sewer and water connections rose from 75% to 98% of total

text.style: font-style: italic; font-size: 7.4px; font-family: 'Lora', 'Newsreader', 'Georgia', 'DejaVu Serif', serif; fill: #8a857b

g.text: households within a decade. The same source records that before the reforms a third of the city's population lived in isolated

text.style: font-style: italic; font-size: 7.4px; font-family: 'Lora', 'Newsreader', 'Georgia', 'DejaVu Serif', serif; fill: #8a857b

g.text: slums without access to clean water or sanitation, but publishes no separate coverage rate for those neighbourhoods, so none is

text.style: font-style: italic; font-size: 7.4px; font-family: 'Lora', 'Newsreader', 'Georgia', 'DejaVu Serif', serif; fill: #8a857b

g.text: shown here. Source: World Bank, Empowerment Case Studies: Participatory Budgeting.
